name: LEGALFLY agents
operator: LEGALFLY (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: LEGALFLY's own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Platform of legal agents (Discovery, Review, Draft, Multi Review, Legal Radar, Translation) plus Agent Studio, where customers build multi-step workflows with triggers, conditions, approvals and notifications.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. From the studio's Web Summit 2026 agents list.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: Two problems. (a) Mode: the Salesforce help article says LEGALFLY must activate the integration on request and each user then connects, so the fact holds only when turned on; it is recorded as default with no cfg. It should be mode available, cfg integrations. (b) Indicator: I07 is 'retrieves information and recommends actions; a person acts'. The article shows Discovery retrieving and summarising Salesforce records and says it cannot create, update or delete; it says nothing about recommending actions. The note itself says only retrieves and summarises. Move to a better-fitting indicator or cut. No level changes: Autonomy 2 would come from I16 anyway, and I07 only counts together with I02 to I05, none of which is answered.

Argued against Autonomy 3 (Acts), the only level three or four on the card (A3 R2 C1 O2). It rests on I08 (workflows page, template 'Multi-Document Review & Redline': 'redlines related documents and emails you the results') and I17 (same page, template 'Legal Helpdesk Triage': 'with Legal approving anything not clearly covered'). Both spans exist verbatim; both are vendor template descriptions on a workflow-library marketing page, two different templates, with no usage figure, no documentation page and no customer named for them. Both are marked available/agent-studio, so the mode is shown honestly (the card prints 'avail available'). Remove either one and Autonomy falls to 2 (I16, default). Many sibling templates on the same page say 'drafts ... for attorney review', which is level two behaviour. The reading is defensible under the rule as written, but the reviewer should know level three is a single page of template blurbs in available mode. Not a must-fix; nothing is wrong with the evidence. The page says 'Start from LEGALFLY pre-built workflows or build your own', which supports available. The page text is in the HTML (not JS-only).

Control 1 rests on I38 alone (I47 is not answered; remove I38 and Control has no level). Indicator I38 is 'High-impact actions need a person's approval'. The span on the Agent Studio page is 'Set approval and review steps where a decision is needed' under 'Human in the loop'. That says a builder can place approval steps; it does not say high-impact actions require one. The mode (available, agent-studio) is correct. Either keep it with a note that it shows the ability to add approval steps (the card's Control 1 'Stated' reads that way), or say why no other indicator fits. Level one is thin but honest if the wording of the note is softened; the note 'Workflow builders can place approval and review steps before a workflow continues' is accurate to the source.

The note says Discovery can search connected folders 'alongside LEGALFLY's own sources'. The integrations page span ('Connect SharePoint and Google Drive to access your documents directly in LEGALFLY.') and the text around it ('let Discovery search your folders without moving documents') do not say 'alongside LEGALFLY's own sources'; I found no such wording on that page. Cut that clause or cite where it is said. The fact itself (connectors to SharePoint and Google Drive, mode available) is right and R2 stands on I11 as well.

The span ('This integration is currently read-only.') is exact and on the Salesforce page, but the note's second clause (security FAQ says anonymisation can hide needed context and how to adjust it) comes from https://www.legalfly.com/security, not the cited source. That URL is a key of captures and the FAQ line is there ('What if anonymisation hides information we need? You can adjust anonymisation levels or whitelist specific terms'), but the answer's source field points elsewhere. State in the note which page says it. The indicator is 'limits and known failure cases are documented'; a read-only limit of one integration is a thin fit, and an FAQ on anonymisation is a product tip, not a failure case. Openness 2 does not depend on I22 (I58 and I61 are two of the three): removing I22 leaves Openness 2.

Span 'Submit a request' (3 words) is on the help centre home page and in the Salesforce article. It is a generic support-request form; the indicator is 'a channel to report problems with it or contest its output'. The page does not say the form is for reporting problems with agent output. Acceptable as documented, but it is the weakest fit in the scan. It feeds no level (Openness 3 also needs I50, which is not answered).

Tier is declared (not public), grade documented. The trust centre lists a request-only document titled 'EU AI Act Article 50 - Technical Documentation and Transparency Information'; the note says the document was not read, which is honest. A document title identifies that a law is considered, which is a loose reading of 'the laws that apply to it are identified'. Q10 is outside the public levels, so it changes no level.

The span is from the June 2026 product highlights post's section on fixed comments: 'When a reviewer applies a suggested redraft during a contract review'. It shows a reviewer applies suggestions; 'each one' in the note is a small step beyond it. The integrations page ('playbooks can be applied with instant redraft suggestions') supports it better. Default mode is plausible for the Review agent. Autonomy 2 is not at risk.

Card (node card.mjs): A3 (I08,I17, available) R2 (I10,I11, available) C1 (I38, available) O2 (I22,I58,I61). Every level except Openness rests on available-mode facts; the card shows this. S1 and S4 are not answered and not in not_credited. S1: the clients page names customers (Nemetschek Group, Duvel Moortgat, Agristo, PIF Group, ECS and others) with outcome figures, but none is tied to Agent Studio workflows (the capability that acts), and the European Commission item says the technology 'will be used', so no In production badge is justified; say so in not_credited. S4: the Salesforce MCP integration is one the product consumes, which does not count; I found no published MCP server, agent card or agent API on any captured page, so Reach 3 is correctly absent. The June blog and the legal-radar page are text in the HTML; the pages were readable without the embedded JSON.

Every URL cited in answers, announced and notes is a key of the scan's 12 captures (compared programmatically; no uncaptured URL). The scan has no not_credited entries. All 13 spans are found exactly in their sources (words, not apostrophe style) and are under fifteen words (max 12). No em-dash, email or at-sign in the scan's prose that I saw.

I20 (agents page: Discovery 'Legally trained agent for research and advice grounded in verified sources', default), I11 (Salesforce MCP integration after per-user authorisation, available), I58 (Legal Radar FAQ lists the types of institutions monitored; narrow, one agent, but it says what it says), I61 (trust centre subprocessors list names Anthropic and OpenAI as AI inference providers with data locations, 'pseudonymised content only, unless a customer explicitly enables' appears for both), I08 and I17 (source says it; grade documented and mode available correct; see level note). Grades are documented throughout; no operation-needing indicator is used.

The four announced items match their sources: Salesforce for other agents 'is planned' (help article), European Commission DG HR 'will be used' (clients page), the Gartner news item and the anonymisation marketing claim (security page, marked not assessed). All four URLs are captured.

The third not_credited entry (I47 and other Control facts, source agentstudio) says no captured page states a log of agent actions, and that the help centre's workflow articles are behind sign-in. The first part is not true of the captured Agent Studio page: under 'Built for regulated enterprises' it says 'Auditable actions: Transparant reasoning, source links and full activity logs' and 'Governed outputs: Playbook enforcement, approvals and role-based access'. The Legal Radar page also says 'keep an audit trail for every compliance action'. I41 needs operation, so a vendor statement cannot earn it and Control stays at 1; the entry should say that (the page claims activity logs, which a statement cannot credit) instead of saying no page states one. The sign-in claim names pages no capture shows (the help centre home capture lists no workflow articles), so it relies on an uncaptured page; cut it or capture the page. The round-one response that this was recorded is therefore only partly true. S1 and S4 entries are correct: the clients page names Nemetschek, Gimpel and others with figures but no tie to Agent Studio workflows, the Commission item reads 'will be used', and Salesforce MCP is consumed.

Response true: the answer now cites Legal Radar, span 'Every update includes a plain-English summary, business impact and recommended next steps' is exact (12 words) and the page continues 'so you know what to do, not just what changed'. Indicator fits. Mode default is asserted but the page does not show whether Legal Radar is included by default or a separate module; it counts only with I02 to I05, none answered, so no level depends on it. Answered.

No change, response argued rather than edited. Its corroboration claim is loose: the template it points to says 'flags the response deadline and drafts a response for attorney review', not that it routes for approval or sets a reminder. The scan does not use that claim, so nothing to fix. See the levels finding.

Card A3 R2 C1 O2 (card.mjs). Argued against Autonomy 3: it needs I08 and one of I17/I18/I19. I08 rests on one template line from a workflow library, 'redlines related documents and emails you the results'; the email goes to the requester, and the redline is a document edit, so it is a thin reading of 'executes actions itself'. I17 rests on another template, 'with Legal approving anything not clearly covered', which does give an exception path. Remove I08 or I17 and Autonomy falls to 2 (I16, default). Both are mode available, cfg agent-studio, and the card shows 'avail available', so the mode is shown honestly; the card does not say that the evidence is two template descriptions with no customer or usage tied to them. Level 4 is not claimed (needs I18, unanswered). Reach 2 stands on I10 and I11 (either alone); Control 1 stands on I38 alone, a statement that a builder can add approval steps; Openness 2 needs two of I22, I58, I61, each narrow (one integration, one agent, a subprocessor list) but any pair satisfies the rule. The publication rule (level one or more in at least one dimension) is met.

Response true: note now reads 'a workflow builder can add approval and review steps at the points where a decision is needed', span 'Set approval and review steps where a decision is needed' exact (10 words) under 'Human in the loop'. It shows ability, not a rule for high-impact actions; Control 1 reads that way. Mode available is right. Answered.

Verified against the live pages. I10: clause removed, note now matches 'let Discovery search your folders without moving documents', span exact (12 words), available. I22: anonymisation clause removed, note states only the read-only limit; span 'This integration is currently read-only.' exact on the Salesforce article, which also says 'it cannot create, update, or delete records'. I16: 'each one' removed; span exact (11 words) on the June 2026 post. All three answered.

Both kept as before with weak fit (generic 'Submit a request' form; a request-only document title for EU AI Act Article 50). The responses are accurate, the spans are exact and in range, and neither feeds a level. Not required to change.

Checked by program: every URL in answers, announced and not_credited is a key of captures (twelve keys, none missing); all fourteen spans are found in their cited source after whitespace and quote normalisation and none exceeds 12 words; no em-dash and no email in the scan (the at-sign appears only in the by fields). Announced items (Salesforce for other agents planned, Commission 'will be used', Gartner news item, anonymisation claim) match their pages. Round one findings I07, I10, I22, I16, I38 and the S1/S4 not_credited entries are answered as stated; only the Control not_credited entry is not.

Argue against Autonomy 3 (A3 R2 C1 O2). I08 now rests on one template card on the workflows page ('drafts a DPIA where high risk is found and updates your register'). It is a vendor description of a template in available mode, and 'updates your register' says what the template does, not that any customer runs it or that it writes without a person checking the draft. I17 rests on one line, 'with Legal approving anything not clearly covered', which describes a helpdesk template that routes to a person. Both are single template blurbs with no customer, no usage and no documentation page; remove either and Autonomy is 2 (I16). The scan says this itself in its round-two response, and the card shows 'avail available', so the reading is defensible and honestly labelled. Publication rule met (level at least one in every dimension).

The third not_credited entry cites the Legal Radar page's audit trail in its text but names only the Agent Studio URL as source. Both pages are captured and both phrases are exact ('full activity logs', 'Governed outputs' on Agent Studio; 'audit trail' on Legal Radar), so no rule is broken; naming the Legal Radar URL in the why text would make it self-contained. Not required.

Changed field verified on a fresh fetch of the workflows page: span 'drafts a DPIA where high risk is found and updates your register' is exact, 12 words, under the New Processing Activity DPIA Assessment template. The note's other examples (emailed redlines, routing drafts for signature) are on the same page ('emails you the results', 'routes them for review and signature'). Indicator I08 (executes actions itself, needs statement) fits; grade documented, mode available, cfg agent-studio correct.

Round two's only should-fix (third not_credited entry) is answered: the entry no longer says no page states an action log, says the Agent Studio page and Legal Radar claim activity logs and an audit trail as product statements that cannot earn I41 (needs operation), and the sign-in clause is gone. Its remaining absence claims (no pause or stop, no written limit) hold: I searched all fetched pages for pause, kill switch, stop or cancel a workflow and found nothing. Round-two notes (I07, I08/I17, I38, I10/I22/I16, I57/I36, S1/S4) are unchanged and still true; the studio's responses match the file. Every URL cited in any note, announced or not_credited entry is a key of the twelve captures (compared programmatically; the only odd hit was a trailing comma in a review finding's text). All 14 spans are found exactly in fresh fetches and are 12 words or fewer; announced items (Salesforce planned, Commission 'will be used', Gartner news item, anonymisation 'only legal AI' claim) match their pages. No em-dash and no email in the scan; the at-sign appears only in by fields. Card via card.mjs: A3 R2 C1 O2.

responses.response: Agreed on both counts: the Salesforce source shows retrieval, not recommendation. I07 now cites the Legal Radar page, which says every update comes with recommended next steps (span verified on the captured page), mode default; no level changes.

Argument answered, no change: both spans are verbatim, the page says customers start from pre-built workflows or build their own, and the same page corroborates acting with an exception path (a template that drafts responses, routes them for approval and sets a deadline reminder). The mode stays available/agent-studio, so the card shows Acts only in that configuration.

Kept at Control 1 in available mode, note softened to what the page says: a builder can add approval and review steps where a decision is needed, which matches Control 1's 'documents say how people approve'. No other indicator fits: no captured page states a prose rule limiting the agents (I47), a pause or stop (I39) or an action log (I41), and the workflow help articles are sign-in only; this is recorded in not_credited.
Cut 'alongside LEGALFLY's own sources'; the note now follows the page ('let Discovery search your folders without moving documents'). Mode and span unchanged.

Removed the anonymisation FAQ clause, which came from the security page; the note now states only the Salesforce read-only limit from the cited article. Kept as a documented user-facing limit; Openness 2 does not depend on it.
Kept as documented; the fit is weak but the help centre's request form is the only public support channel found, and it feeds no level.
Kept; the note already says only the document title was read, and Q10 is outside the public levels.
Removed 'each one'; the note now says the agent suggests redrafts and a reviewer applies a suggested redraft, as the post says. Autonomy 2 unchanged.

Added not_credited entries for S1 (customers named but none tied to Agent Studio workflows; the Commission item is future tense) and S4 (the Salesforce MCP is consumed, not published), plus the absent Control facts.
Still holds: every source in the edits and not_credited is a key of the scan's captures, and the one new span (Legal Radar) is verbatim, 12 words, no em-dash.
No change.
No change.

Agreed. The third not_credited entry is rewritten: it now says the Agent Studio page claims full activity logs (and Legal Radar an audit trail), which as product statements cannot earn I41 (needs operation), and keeps only the absences that hold on the captured pages (no pause or stop, no written limit). The sign-in clause is cut because it relied on a help article that is not among the scan's captures; Control stays 1.
No change. Mode default is as the Legal Radar page presents the agent; as the finding notes, I07 feeds no level without I02 to I05.

Clarified, no change to I17: the round-one corroboration referred to the Tax Notice template ('routes them for approval and sets a deadline reminder', exact on the page), not the Office Action template; it shows routing and a reminder, not an exception path, so it is not cited for I17. I17 rests on the Helpdesk Triage line, with the NDA Fast Track template ('with legal escalation if required') as a second exception path on the same page.

Answered with evidence, not conceded: I08 now cites a workflow that writes to a system of record ('drafts a DPIA where high risk is found and updates your register', exact, 12 words), alongside emailing redlined documents and routing drafts for signature on the same page, and the Agent Studio page says 'Conditional logic automatically routes work, triggers follow-ups, and escalates when thresholds are met'. Conceded in part: all of this is vendor description of available templates with no customer or usage tied to them, which is why both I08 and I17 stay documented, mode available, cfg agent-studio, and S1 stays not credited; Autonomy 3 holds only in the Agent studio configuration.
No change; Control 1 reads as ability in available mode, as the finding says.
No change; verified pass.
No change; neither feeds a level.

Still holds: the new I08 span and both quoted phrases in the rewritten not_credited entry were checked verbatim on fresh fetches of the workflows and Agent Studio pages (raw/ans-001, ans-002), each under 15 words, no em-dash; both sources are existing capture keys.

I07.n: Legal Radar monitors regulatory updates and gives each one a summary, its business impact and recommended next steps for the team to act on.
I07.span: Every update includes a plain-English summary, business impact and recommended next steps

I08.n: The workflow library describes pre-built Agent Studio workflows that act on their results, such as updating a processing register, emailing redlined documents and routing drafts for signature.
I08.span: drafts a DPIA where high risk is found and updates your register

I10.n: SharePoint and Google Drive can be connected so that Discovery searches the customer's folders without moving the documents.
I10.span: Connect SharePoint and Google Drive to access your documents directly in LEGALFLY.

I11.n: Discovery connects to a customer's Salesforce org through an MCP integration after per-user authorisation.
I11.span: Through the Discovery agent's Salesforce MCP integration

I16.n: In Review the agent suggests redrafts during a contract review and a reviewer applies a suggested redraft.
I16.span: When a reviewer applies a suggested redraft during a contract review

I17.n: A pre-built workflow answers routine mailbox questions and sends anything not covered to Legal for approval.
I17.span: with Legal approving anything not clearly covered

I20.n: Each agent's purpose is stated on the agents page, for example Discovery for research and advice.
I20.span: Legally trained agent for research and advice grounded in verified sources

I22.n: The help centre states a limit for users: Discovery's Salesforce integration reads records and cannot create, update or delete them.

I36.n: The trust centre lists a request-only document titled for EU AI Act Article 50 transparency information, which identifies that provision; the document itself was not read.
I36.span: EU AI Act Article 50 - Technical Documentation and Transparency Information

I38.n: In Agent Studio a workflow builder can add approval and review steps at the points where a decision is needed.
I38.span: Set approval and review steps where a decision is needed

I57.n: The public help centre offers a way to submit a request to LEGALFLY support.

I58.n: The sources Legal Radar monitors are described by type of institution.
I58.span: We monitor the published updates from a jurisdiction's main institutions

I61.n: The trust centre lists subprocessors, including Anthropic and OpenAI as AI inference providers, with data locations.
I61.span: Processes pseudonymised content only, unless a customer explicitly enables

not_credited.why: The clients page names customers with outcome figures, but none is tied to Agent Studio workflows, the capability that acts; the European Commission item says the technology will be used, which is not use.

not_credited.what: S4 (a published agent interface: MCP server, agent card or agent API)
not_credited.why: The Salesforce MCP integration is one the product consumes; no captured page describes an MCP server, agent card or API that LEGALFLY publishes for its agents.

not_credited.what: I41 action log, I39 pause or stop, I47 written limits (Control above level 1)
not_credited.why: The Agent Studio page lists 'full activity logs' and 'Governed outputs' and the Legal Radar page an audit trail for compliance actions, but these are product statements; I41 needs an observed log, and no captured page states a way to pause or stop a running workflow or a written rule limiting what the agents may do.

announced.what: Salesforce support in agents other than Discovery is planned
European Commission DG HR deployment: technology 'will be used' for HR legal workflows
Gartner named LEGALFLY a key vendor in agentic AI for legal (company's news item; Gartner report not read)
Marketing claim of being the only legal AI that anonymises before analysis (not assessed)

configurations.note: LEGALFLY legal AI agents with Agent Studio with its documented defaults.
